subtopic: KV cache quantization / Attention kernel compatibility
learningObjective: Identify the kernel-support requirements for KV cache quantization to be effective for both memory and bandwidth savings.
stem: For KV cache quantization to deliver both memory-footprint and memory-bandwidth savings in attention, which of the following statements about kernel support are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: If the attention kernel expects FP16 KVs and the storage is INT8, the kernel must dequantize INT8 → FP16 in registers on the fly; this saves KV storage but adds dequant instructions per attention step (still bandwidth-net-positive because HBM traffic drops).
If the attention kernel is written to consume quantized KVs natively (e.g., FP8 attention on Hopper, or INT8 attention kernels), both storage AND read bandwidth are reduced without dequant overhead.
Storing INT8 KVs but transposing them to FP16 in a separate kernel before attention (an eager dequant) eliminates the bandwidth savings — the same FP16 buffer is then read by the attention kernel.
KV cache quantization requires the model weights to also be quantized to the same precision; mixed-precision (FP16 weights + INT8 KV) is not supported by any framework.
The attention kernel can process quantized KVs with different scales per head, but each head's KVs must share a single scale across all context positions to avoid runtime metadata overhead.

explanation: A: dequant-in-register is the most common pattern (used by TensorRT-LLM's INT8 KV attention); it saves HBM traffic while adding cheap dequant ops. B: native quantized attention (FP8 on Hopper via FlashAttention-3, INT8 attention variants) avoids dequant overhead. C: eager dequant to FP16 defeats the bandwidth benefit — the same-size FP16 buffer is still read by attention. D is false: mixed-precision (FP16 weights + INT8 KV) is common and supported. E is false: per-token / per-head-per-token scaling is the norm; single scale per head is coarser and hurts accuracy.

optionExplanations.C: Correct: eager dequant defeats bandwidth benefit.
optionExplanations.E: Wrong: per-token scaling is the norm.

assumptions: The attention kernel is FlashAttention-family (single-kernel over K and V) or paged-attention.
The framework supports per-token or per-block-per-token scaling.
nonImplications: Does not imply FP8 KV is always better than INT8 KV — depends on hardware and distribution.
Does not imply dequant-in-register is free — for very small heads it may become a noticeable fraction of the kernel.

distractorRationales.D: Fabricates a coupling between KV and weight precision.
distractorRationales.E: Overrestricts scale-granularity to a coarser level.

sourceRefs.locator: INT8 / FP8 KV cache kernel implementation
